Although there's excitement and merriment at first, Baba soon becomes unsure about sleeping so far from home.

Chan eil an gnothach cho furasta 's a bha iad an dùil ge-tà, gu h-àraidh dha Baba beag bochd! When sleeping over with the Hoots, Oona and Baba realise that they must sleep during the day, just like their owl friends. However, the reality of getting to sleep in the middle of the day isn't so easy, especially for poor Baba.

Anns a’ phrògram seo tha Eilidh a’ cèilidh air Leo is Dara agus Bòtannan, an cat eireachdail aca. Gheibh sinn a-mach barrachd mu bhith a’ coimhead às dèidh cait agus mu na rudan snog is spòrsail a bhios Leo is Dara agus Bòtannan a’ dèanamh còmhla. Gheibh sinn cuideachd comhairle agus fiosrachadh bho Eilidh fhèin mu bhith a’ làimhseachadh, ag oideachadh agus a’ coimhead às dèidh peataichean. Eilidh Cormack meets young children who are pet owners. Together, they show, tell and share how they care for, play and interact with their pets at home. In this episode, Eilidh visits Leo and Dara and their handsome cat Bòtannan. We find out how to look after cats and about all the lovely stuff Leo, Dara and Bòtannan get up to together. Eilidh also shares fun and interesting facts along with advice on looking after pets at home - including how best to handle, train and feed them.

Thòisich Julie Fleeting a’ cluiche ball-coise còmhla ri sgioba bhalaich aig naoi bliadhna a dh’aois, a’ chiad cheum air an t-slighe gu dreuchd nach robh i fiù’s a smaointinn a bha comasach dhith. programme.title: Belladrum
programme.desc: Tha Fiona NicChoinnich agus Niall Iain Dòmhnallach a’ cur fàilt’ air Toby Lee gu Àrd-Ùrlar Hot House aig Belladrum 2025. Ged nach eil Toby ach 20 bliadhna a dh’aois, tha na sàr-sgilean cluiche agus a ghuth iongantach air cothroman fhuasgladh dha air an àrd-ùrlar leis an luchd-ciùil as fheàrr – mar Buddy Guy, Billy Gibbons, Peter Frampton, Slash agus Joe Bonamassa. Fiona MacKenzie and Niall Iain Macdonald welcome Toby Lee to the Hot House Stage at Belladrum. A mind-blowing guitarist and a voice to match, the 20-year-old’s music belies his age and has seen him sharing the stage with the best in the business, including Buddy Guy, Billy Gibbons, Peter Frampton, Slash and Joe Bonamassa.

A’ comharrachadh 15 bliadhna mar chòmhlan, thug Trail West cuireadh do an caraidean ceòlmhor gu ‘dachaigh rock & roll’ agus rinn an luchd-leantainn an slighe chun an talla-ciùil as cliùitiche ann an Glaschu airson a’ phàrtaidh as fheàrr air a’ Chost’ an Iar. A special concert from the Barrowland Ballroom featuring performances from Trail West, Beinn Lee and Ruairidh Gray. Celebrating 15 years as a band, Trail West invited their musical pals to 'the home of rock and roll', so their fans descended on Glasgow’s most iconic venue for the ultimate west coast party. In Gaelic with English subtitles.

Tha an dìsinn a’ còrdadh ri Comhachag agus tha e a’ dèanamh iomlaid air a shon leis an dèideag as fheàrr leis. Tha Sionnach air a dhòigh leis an dèideag ùr ach tha Comhachag ga h-ionndrainn gu mòr. Chan eil guth aig Sionnach air a toirt air ais gus an smaoinich Maigheach ghleusta air dòigh anns an toir i a’ chomhstrì gu ceann. Fox finds a giant dice in a box of discarded belongings. Owl really likes it too and decides to trade it for his favourite doll, Oehoe. Fox enjoys life with his new toy, but Owl comes to realise he made a huge mistake; he misses Oehoe so much! Fox, however, won’t give it back. Hare thinks of a cunning way to solve the stand-off.

Tha Ms Sharpe agus cuid de na sgoilearan aice trang ag ullachadh airson a’ Mhòid, agus chan eil cùisean idir rèidh eadar Danny agus Mrs Fullerton. As the first term comes to an end, it’s evident that tensions are building at Sgoil Taobh na Cloiche. Miss Sharpe and her pupils are busy preparing for the Mòd and it’s looking as if Danny and Mrs Fullerton are out for revenge.

programme.title: Calum: Cogadh nan Comhlan
programme.desc: Tha Calum airson a chòmhlann aige a thoirt à Glaschu dhan Òban airson blàr mòr ciùil a tha dol aig a' Mhòd Nàiseanta Rìoghail. Ach, le tòrr fharpaisean agus gainead tìde, chan eil cùisean a' dol mar bu chòir. Leis nach eil e furasda còmhlan a làimhseachadh aig na h-amannan as fheàrr, saoil ciamar a thèid dhaibh leis na dùbhlain mhòra a th' air thoiseach orra... Calum aims to take his band from Glasgow to Oban for a major musical battle at the Royal National Mòd. However, with numerous competitions and time constraints, things aren't going according to plan. Managing a band is never easy even in the best of times - how will they cope with the significant challenges that lie ahead?

An e “slime” cruasbach, “slime” a ghabhas ithe, “slime” bith-chnàmhach no “slime” molach? Choirstaidh is looking for the best slime recipe, but what will it be? Crunchy, edible, biodegradable or fluffy slime?

programme.title: Rurachd (Foraging)
programme.desc: Màiri Anna NicUalraig agus Liusaidh Cooke – An Còcaire Fiadhain – a’ rùrachd airson tairbheartas nàdair. Tha Liusaidh a’ toirt Màiri Anna dhachaigh gu dùthaich a h-òige, Shropshire, far an do thòisich a beatha an co-bhuinn ri nàdar. Tha iad a’ trusadh bhalgan-buachair nach gabh a lorg an Gàidhealtachd na h-Alba, agus a’ dèanamh picil leotha. Tha iad a’ beachdachadh air àrainneachd gu math eadar-dhealaichte bho an dachaigh an Alba le taic bho athair Liusaidh, a’ tadhal air darach a tha co-dhiù 800 bliadhn’ a dh’aois, agus a’ trusadh eidheann-thalmhainn, lus cùbhraidh a tha càirdeach do phionnd is sèids. Agus tha an còmhnaidh ùine ann airson basgaid ùir. Mary Ann Kennedy and Lucy Cooke - The Wild Cooke -forage for nature’s bounty. Lucy takes Mary Ann to Shropshire where she grew up and began her life in harmony with nature. They collect fungi that can’t be found in Highland Scotland and pickle them. With some help from Lucy’s dad, they visit an 800-year-old oak tree and forage for ground ivy, a fragrant herb related to mint and sage. And there’s always time for a new basket. In Gaelic with English subtitles

programme.title: Faodail
programme.desc: Tha Tasglann Fhilm Faodail a’ tarraing aire gu filmichean dhùthchasach Innse Gall bho na 1930an gu na 80an, a bha caillte ach a-nis glèidhte don ghinealach ri teachd. Tha bhana Cinema Sgìre Leantainneach a’ siubhal nan eilean, a’ taisbeanadh fhilmichean sna sgìrean ionadail, le cothrom am faicinn air-loidhne air feadh an t-saoghail. Cuirear aithris bheairteach ùr riutha, a’ buntainn ris a’ Ghàidhealtachd, airson luchd-amhairc an là an-diugh. The Faodail Film Archive celebrates lost indigenous film collections from the 1930s to the 1980s in the Outer Hebrides, preserving the archive for future generations. The Cinema Sgìre Continuing mobile cinema van travels the islands, showcasing footage to local communities, making them accessible globally online, and adding rich new narratives relevant to the Gàidhealtachd for contemporary audiences. In Gaelic with English subtitles.

Anns an dàrna prògram mu dheireadh san t-sreath, tha nighean Aonghais, Rut, còmhla ris agus iad aig muir air latha samhraidh eireachdail. Air an t-slighe, coinnichidh iad ri buidheann leumadairean-mara a tha dannsa mun eathar. Às dèidh sin, tha an t-àm ann airson iasgach agus còmhradh mun bhuaidh a bh’ aig iasgach air beatha Ruth.

programme.desc: In September 1977, police attend a house in Enfield, London, to investigate a reported home invasion. There had been loud knocking on the wall and furniture moved. The two officers can find no evidence of a break-in, but they do hear rapping on the walls, see furniture tilt independently and a chair slide several metres across the room on its own. This is to be the first of many extraordinary events that have been recorded on film and audio tape, culminating in disembodied voices and levitation. To this day, the activities remain difficult to explain.

programme.title: Hauntings
programme.desc: When Andrea Perron moves into her new home in Rhode Island with her parents and four sisters, the previous occupants seem in a hurry to leave. Their investigations lead to a séance, which changes the lives of the Perron family.

programme.title: Asteroids: Spark of Life?
programme.desc: Imagine a time about four billion years ago when the newly formed Earth was a molten, volcanic wasteland, constantly bombarded by colossal asteroids. Asteroids much larger than the one that wiped out the dinosaurs. But what if these destructive cosmic impacts were the key to our very existence? Scientists are exploring the deep past embedded in South African and Australian rocks, the surface of the moon, asteroid dust taken from space and ancient impact craters to develop a revolutionary new theory that suggests these violent collisions may have provided the essential ingredients – water, minerals and energy – needed for life to ignite on our planet. Could the very objects once thought to extinguish life have actually sparked it?
